name: Jeroham
overview: Jeroham was a male figure known from the biblical account as one of those who came to David at Ziklag. He is uniquely identified as being from Gedor, which situates him geographically within the narrative. No tribal affiliation is recorded for him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroham means 'he will be compassionate,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew proper name. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a significant attribute of mercy or compassion.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Jeroham was the son of Joelah and also the son of Zebadiah, though these relationships are not explicitly detailed beyond the reference in 1 Chronicles 12:7. No further family connections are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroham's significance lies in his association with David during a critical period when David was gathering support at Ziklag. Coming from Gedor, Jeroham represents one of the individuals who aligned with David, contributing to the consolidation of David's leadership. His presence in the biblical record underscores the diverse support David received from various regions and families.
